headline: UK committee chair asks Anthropic for the unredacted METR acceleration report
body: Liam Byrne, who chairs the House of Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee, made the request in a letter dated November 27, wanting a complete, unredacted copy of METR's November 5 report, by December 4. The Decoder reports that METR has said publicly that Anthropic cut major parts of the report before publication.
note: Banks and insurers that lean on lab-published safety evaluations when approving models will want to know how much of the evidence readers actually get to see.

evidence.text: Liam Byrne, who chairs the House of Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee, made the request in a letter dated November 27 .
Byrne wants a complete, unredacted copy of METR's November 5 report on how fast AI research and development at Anthropic was accelerating in October.
METR , an AI safety organization, has said publicly that Anthropic cut major parts of the report before publication, including much of the evidence the group called "most informative."
Byrne, whose inquiry centers on AI safety, wants the redacted material by December 4, along with an explanation of why it was redacted.
